messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - elevated 5xx and request queueing observed for us-east -> provider-a. Error rate crossed 8% over 2m, latency p95 spiked to 1.8s. Automatic provider failover attempted and partially succeeded, some sessions still routing to provider-a. Auto-drain started for some hosts at 1801001950. Paging on-call infra.
Alex Chen: on it. seeing a surge of long tail client connections to provider-a edge. starting manual traffic shaping to shed non-critical routes.
Priya Patel: Alex, can you confirm which routes are non-critical? I can flip rate-limits on the gateway while you adjust weights.
Alex Chen: marking /embeddings-batch and /bulk-async as low-priority. plan: 1) apply soft rate-limit 50rps per-customer on those routes 2) reduce provider-a weight to 30% for realtime routes 3) enable regional failover for high-priority customers to provider-b.
Sven Müller: runtime note: if we reduce model-variant fanouts we can drop memory pressure on provider-a. I'll push a quick config to disable experimental-quantized-16 variant on provider-a pool.
Maya Li: CS reporting 3 SOC customers seeing errors for long-running batch jobs. Prioritize giving them ETA and mitigation details. I'll draft message.
Ben Ward: product: agree with shedding non-critical routes. Also want to flag that canary users on dedicated capacity might be affected if we change routing; please list impacted customer segments.
Alex Chen: executing step 1 now: applying rate-limit via gateway service.
Alex Chen: ```
# curl to API gateway admin
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://gw-admin.us-east.internal/ratelimits \
  -d '{"route":"/embeddings-batch","limit_rps":50,"scope":"per-customer"}'
```
incident-bot: Action recorded: rate-limit applied to /embeddings-batch (50rps) by Alex Chen at 1801002022.
Priya Patel: I'm lowering provider-a weight for realtime routes to 30% in the routing service. Command:
```
rbctl route set-weight --route realtime --provider provider-a --weight 30
rbctl route set-weight --route realtime --provider provider-b --weight 70
```
Sven Müller: pushed runtime flag to disable experimental variant on provider-a: `runtime-config set provider-a disable-quant-16 true` . Monitoring heap and kv-cache evictions.
Alex Chen: observability: errors on provider-a dropped from 8.3% -> 4.1% in ~60s, but some 5xx still persist for long sessions. p95 still ~1.1s. Throughput on provider-b increased as expected.
Priya Patel: I'm enabling a short partial brownout for non-real-time webhooks by returning 429 with Retry-After for 30s bursts, to protect realtime traffic.
Priya Patel: ```
# brownout rule
config set brownout:webhooks non_critical=true retry_after=30
```
Maya Li: CS update sent to affected customers: "We're mitigating elevated errors by rerouting realtime traffic and temporarily limiting lower-priority batch jobs. Expect reduced errors within minutes. Contact ops@redwood for urgent escalations." They asked for per-customer impact list.
Alex Chen: creating impacted list: will export from routing logs for last 10m.
Alex Chen: ```
# quick query
logsq "route:embeddings-batch AND provider:provider-a" --since 10m --fields customer_id | uniq
```
Ben Ward: please tag any enterprise customers; we may need to open a dedicated bridge.
incident-bot: Bridge created: https://meet.redwood/incident/1801002000
Sven Müller: FYI, provider-a reported a partial NAT gateway saturation on their side earlier - they're investigating. This matches some of the TCP resets we saw.
Priya Patel: Considering a forced regional failover for high priority routes: flip us-east realtime traffic to provider-b completely, keep provider-a at 0 for realtime while they heal. Anyone object?
Ben Ward: go for it for high priority. coordinate with CS for customer notices.
Alex Chen: initiating failover for realtime routes. Command:
```
rbctl route set-weight --route realtime --provider provider-a --weight 0
rbctl route set-weight --route realtime --provider provider-b --weight 100
```
incident-bot: Failover action applied at 1801002125 by Alex Chen. Routing change propagated to 85% of edge nodes in 20s; remaining nodes scheduling update.
Alex Chen: observing final propagation. p95 realtime latency now 420ms, errors down to 0.9%.
Maya Li: CS: pushed updated note to enterprise customers, offered 1:1 bridge for any who need deeper postmortem.
Priya Patel: adding quota bump in provider-b for short term to handle extra load: bump per-node connections by 20%.
Priya Patel: ```
cloudctl provider-b quota update --connections-per-node +20%
```
Sven Müller: runtime warning: kv-cache miss rate increased 2x on provider-b after ramp. Might need to enable prefix cache warmup on provider-b to avoid latency regressions.
Alex Chen: enabling prefix warmup script now. ```scripts/prefix-warmup --targets provider-b --prefixes /chat /realtime``` will run for 5m.
incident-bot: Warmup started at 1801002180.
Priya Patel: once warmup completes, monitor tail-latency, we should be able to re-enable a small portion of background jobs.
Alex Chen: warmup complete at 1801002300. tail-latency improved. Re-enabling low-priority routes at 30% on provider-b only.
Alex Chen: ```rbctl route set-weight --route embeddings-batch --provider provider-b --weight 30
rbctl route set-weight --route embeddings-batch --provider provider-a --weight 0
``` 
Priya Patel: confirm background batch errors are stable. If they spike, we revert to full block.
Maya Li: CS reporting one SOC customer still seeing timeouts on a historical batch - likely queued job that hit the old provider-a backend. They requested job retry policy.
Ben Ward: product to follow-up on job retry semantics. For now advise customers to re-submit; we'll provide a short window to auto-retry where safe.
Alex Chen: handoff note for next on-call: we've stabilized realtime traffic by failing over to provider-b, partial brownout for non-critical routes remains in place, rate-limits applied, provider-a is currently drained for realtime. Provider-a team reports investigating NAT saturation. If provider-a is healthy in 30m, we can consider gradual re-weight.
Alex Chen: tagging @oncall-ops for handoff.
oncall-ops: ack. taking over monitoring. will escalate to provider contacts if provider-a doesn't report improvement within 45m. Updating post-incident doc and starting timeline.
incident-bot: Incident P1 moved to monitoring at 1801002360. All major mitigations implemented. Please update postmortem checklist: root_cause, mitigation_timeline, customer_impact_list, followups.
Maya Li: compiling customer impact list and outreach log; will attach to the postmortem.
Alex Chen: final note: avoid making config changes to routing weight outside the bridge. I'll add a brief runbook snippet to the incident doc:
```
# Emergency failover steps (short)
1) Identify high-priority routes: realtime, chat, web-rtc
2) Apply weight 0 to failing provider for those routes
3) Enable brownout for non-critical routes
4) Warmup cache on target provider
5) Monitor p95 and 5xx for 10m
6) Gradually bring back background jobs
```
Ben Ward: thanks team. I'll schedule a 1hr post-incident review with runtime and provider vendor tomorrow.
incident-bot: Thread closed for active mitigation at 1801002380. Reminder: create postmortem within 48h. :white_check_mark:
